source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 is a mid-sized Virginia data center, not a frontier AI site: 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, ranking 26th among Virginia facilities that publish capacity.

The scale is the story. At 11 MW the facility sits outside the state's top tier and accounts for under 1% of Virginia's disclosed capacity of 1,603 MW. The data center's own description emphasizes network connectivity, with multiple metro and long-haul circuits, which matters for distributed training and inference where data movement, not raw power, is the constraint. That profile fits enterprise and inference workloads better than large training runs, which cluster where hundreds of megawatts are available on one campus.

The limit of what this tells you is the denominator. Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, and only 25 publish capacity figures. The other 305 are invisible in this data, so the state's true aggregate capacity, and whether larger campuses sit near Sterling, cannot be judged from this record. A single facility's published number says nothing about the unpublished ones beside it.

The location is the one hard geographic fact: 3.2 miles from Washington Dulles International Airport, in Sterling, in the densest data center market in the world. Proximity to fiber routes and an airport explains why a facility this size exists there at all. Power, not land or connectivity, is what would cap it.
